facts.statement: Parabohaiornis is an extinct bird belonging to the Enantiornithes clade, specifically the Bohaiornithidae family, found in northeastern China.
facts.quote: Parabohaiornis is an extinct genus of bohaiornithid enantiornithean dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: The genus Parabohaiornis was named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor, and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014.
facts.quote: Parabohaiornis was first described and named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014

facts.statement: The name Parabohaiornis means "close to Bohaiornis", referring to its morphological similarity to that genus.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Latin prefix para, meaning "close to", with the generic name of Bohaiornis

facts.statement: The species name martini honors the paleontologist Larry Dean Martin for his work on bird evolution.
facts.quote: The specific name, martini, honors the late paleontologist Prof. Larry Dean Martin

facts.statement: Fossils of Parabohaiornis were collected near Lamadong Town in Jianchang County, Liaoning Province, from the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The specimens were collected at deposits near the Lamadong Town, Jianchang County of the Liaoning Province, from the Jiufotang Formation

facts.statement: Parabohaiornis possessed three teeth in the premaxilla and four teeth in the maxilla.
facts.quote: It has three and four teeth on the premaxilla and maxilla, respectively.

facts.statement: Unlike related genera, Parabohaiornis lacks a maxillary process on its nasal bone.
facts.quote: Unlike Longusunguis, Zhouornis and Sulcavis, its nasal bone lacks a maxillary process.

facts.statement: The acromion process of Parabohaiornis is straight and parallel to the scapular shaft, unlike the deflected process seen in other bohaiornithids.
facts.quote: In Parabohaiornis, the acromion process is straight, and is parallel to the scapular shaft

facts.statement: Parabohaiornis has a unique pygostyle-to-third-metatarsal length ratio ranging from 0.92 to 0.99.
facts.quote: Parabohaiornis has a distinctive length ratio of the pygostyle to the third metatarsal of 0.92–0.99

facts.statement: In Parabohaiornis, the proximal phalanx of the fourth digit is less than 70% the length of the penultimate phalanx.
facts.quote: in Parabohaiornis it is much shorter (less than 70%)

facts.statement: The known specimens of Parabohaiornis are preserved in single slabs and housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing.
facts.quote: Both specimens are preserved in single slabs and are currently housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Beijing.

facts.statement: Both known specimens of Parabohaiornis represent subadult individuals, with the referred specimen being more mature than the holotype.
facts.quote: Both specimen came from subadult individuals, the referred being more mature than the holotype

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Parabohaiornis as an advanced bohaiornithid closely related to the genus Bohaiornis.
facts.quote: Parabohaiornis was recovered as an advanced bohaiornithid, closely related to Bohaiornis

facts.statement: The fossil record for Parabohaiornis spans the Aptian stage from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
